messages:
alex: Heads-up — eu-west2 GPU pool is at sustained pressure (avg util 92% across recent 5m window) and we're getting a noisy stream of low-severity eviction alerts that are waking the rotation. I'm proposing a short-lived suppression + graceful deprioritization policy so oncall can triage real failovers instead of paging for transient evictions. Thoughts? :thinking_face:
maria: Can you paste the metric links and current alert counts? want to make sure we're not hiding anything critical.
sam: +1 for suppression if we keep a hard escalation path. Maybe reroute low-priority inference traffic to eu-west1 burst pool or to a cpu fallback while we drain the queue. That avoids customer impact.
alex: Metric: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/GPUPool/eu-west2?from=now-15m to=now — eviction.low firing 37x in last 10m, eviction.critical 0. Most evictions are in a single AZ. Autoscaler logs show recent preemptible churn.
kyra: If we suppress, we should change pagerbot behavior: suppress severity=warning for 20m, but auto-escalate if the same alert persists beyond 20m or rate > 8/min. Also add a note to the runbook to check preemptible churn and migrate urgent traffic.
devon: cost question: rerouting to burst reserved pools will increase unit cost. estimate: ~+12% token cost for affected requests for the next hour. okay for SLO windows?
alex: We have 30% slack across dedicated pools; prefer burst routing there first. If we hit dedicated, fall back to cpu fallback. I'll draft the routing rule.
sam: Draft routing rule suggestion:
```yaml
routing:
  - name: eu-west2-lowprio-divert
    match: traffic.priority == "low" and model.size <= "small"
    action:
      - send_to: eu-west1-burst
      - fallback: cpu-fallback-pool
    timeout: 60s
```
kyra: pagerbot config I'm going to test in staging: (small snippet)
```yaml
pagerbot:
  suppressions:
    - alert: eviction.low
      duration: 20m
      escalate_if: "persist > 20m or rate > 8/min"
      notify_channel: #eng-oncall
```
maria: Make sure we keep audit logs of suppressed pages and include who acknowledged. we need the correlation ids for post-incident review.
ops-bot: pagerbot: queued change detected. Applying suppression rule to eu-west2 for alert `eviction.low` for 20m. Change id: ch_196850_01.
devon: Who's triaging while this suppression is active? we still need a human in the loop for runbook steps.
alex: I'll take the triage window for the next 30m, then hand off to sam at 10:30 UTC. sam: ok, I can take over at 10:30. alex -> sam handoff noted.
sam: quick checklist I'll follow: 1) verify eviction origin AZ, 2) kick a graceful drain on noisy nodes, 3) kick autoscaler cooldown tweak (extend cooldown from 90s to 180s for preemptible pools), 4) start reroute if evictions continue.
kyra: added a one-line runbook edit in staging: `If eviction.low fires >3x in 10m, suppress pages 20m and trigger routing rule; escalate to critical if persists 20m`. please review: https://git.redwood/runbooks/eu-west2/gpu-evictions.md
ops-bot: deploybot: runbook doc updated in staging branch `eviction-suppress-196850` — CI passed.
maria: After suppression ends, please post a summary here (counts suppressed, reroute bytes, CPU-fallback tokens, cost delta). We need that for SRE weekly review.
alex: Will do. Summary will include metrics + decision checklist.
pagerbot: suppression active for `eviction.low` (eu-west2) until +20m. Will auto-escalate if rule conditions hit.
sam: taking over triage at 10:30 UTC. alex hands off. leaving a quick note: checked node churn logs, looks like host-level preemptions spiked. starting graceful drains now. :white_check_mark:
alex: thanks, team. updating handoff notes and will follow-up in postmortem if needed.
kyra: small follow-up: recommend adding a short-term anomaly detector to detect preemption spikes and auto-trigger routing instead of purely alert-suppression. filing a ticket: TKT-9843.
maria: fine by me. keep pages minimal but preserve escalation path. good job for moving fast. :thumbsup:
